evidence_note: Summaries of prior source reviews, not a new pixel inspection. Observations are attributed to the recorded reviewer; inference is design interpretation, not author intent. Links only; no source media redistributed.

observed: The first call feeds a violet gate; its passing route bends upward through two later calls to the output.
A dashed failing branch descends to a separate exit. Intermediate outputs are labeled on the main path.
records.inference: A visible negative outcome counters the common optimistic assumption that every input reaches the final call. A distinct control color separates checking from generation.
records.rule: Preserve the negative branch of a decision. Name intermediate artifacts so dependency is intelligible.
records.limit: Independent benefits are not a serial chain. An unspecified decorative gate does not explain validation.

observed: A router leads to three vertically aligned call boxes and a shared output; there is no aggregator card.
One route is solid and other routes are dashed. The peer-box arrangement resembles the neighboring parallelization example.
records.inference: Keeping the worker silhouette familiar makes the absence of an aggregator significant when the gallery is compared. Dashes need explanation because they could otherwise mean uncertainty or failure.
records.rule: Differentiate alternatives from concurrency using topology and labels. Use stable geometry across comparable pattern figures.
records.limit: Do not use exclusive dispatch when every branch contributes to one result. Dashed routes do not encode measured probabilities.

observed: Solid connectors fan from the input into three equal green peer boxes.
All worker outputs enter a violet aggregator before the final output. The join is a named processing card, not merely intersecting lines.
records.inference: The explicit aggregator makes reconciliation visible and distinguishes this figure from routing, even though both contain three worker boxes.
records.rule: Name a join when it evaluates or reconciles results. Verify independence before depicting parallel branches.
records.limit: A later task that needs an earlier result belongs in a chain. Equal cards do not show equal effort or reliability.

observed: Generator and evaluator exchange a solution on an upper curved path and rejection/feedback on a lower return path.
An accepted branch leaves toward an output distinct from the cycle.
records.inference: Opposing labeled arcs reduce confusion about who produces the criterion. A visible accepted exit keeps iteration from appearing unbounded.
records.rule: Give both directions of a feedback loop distinct labels. Expose termination and escalation conditions.
records.limit: Repeated independent sampling without actionable feedback is a different pattern. Iteration count cannot be presented as quality improvement without evidence.

observed: Large chat and system panels are linked by user-request and final-report arrows.
A central lead agent connects to memory, a citation agent and three search subagents below, with return paths and self-loops.
records.inference: Keeping citation and memory roles visible plausibly prevents reducing the system to a search fan-out. The chat boundary makes internal exchanges distinct from user-visible outputs.
records.rule: Separate user-facing and internal exchanges. Keep persistence and provenance roles visible when they affect the result.
records.limit: Central card size is not resource consumption. This map does not determine message timing.

records.relationship: iterative research; persistence; final citation processing
observed: Seven lifelines separate user, system, lead, two subagents, memory and citation roles.
A large tinted research-loop region contains repeated exchanges and self-loops; citation processing and the final report occur later.
records.inference: The enclosure makes repeated investigation legible but increases density. This is a zoomable detail view, not an appropriate small thumbnail or sole overview.
records.rule: Separate iteration from finalization. Use coordinated overview/detail views at different reading scales.
records.limit: Loop regions do not guarantee convergence. Spacing and panel height are not execution duration.

observed: The simpler left panel shows prompt-to-model-to-message. The wider right panel adds documents, tools, memory/history and a dashed current-context boundary.
Information cards and selection marks identify curation, while tool activity returns information to history.
records.inference: Stable model/output grammar reduces comparison effort. The added resources alone do not establish improved results, so the new design should emphasize selection rather than accumulation.
records.rule: Hold familiar components constant in a conceptual comparison. Distinguish available information from information actually loaded.
records.limit: More documents do not automatically improve results. Wider or more colorful panels are not quantitative superiority evidence.

observed: A tiled horizontal band uses orange ends and a green middle. Three markers connect to examples of different textual density.
Labels distinguish excessive specificity, a useful middle and vagueness; no numeric axis establishes an optimum.
records.inference: Same-task examples isolate specificity from topic. Green emphasis makes the recommendation obvious but risks implying a tested universal optimum without a conceptual label.
records.rule: Calibrate with the same task at multiple levels of detail. Label conceptual scales explicitly.
records.limit: Marker spacing does not quantify performance. A generic middle-ground rule cannot relax exact safety requirements.

records.relationship: source document; fragment enrichment; unchanged indexing
observed: A wider preparation panel shows a whole document, selected blue chunks and context generation.
Blue context-plus-chunk pairs feed otherwise neutral indexing; a small runtime region retains orientation.
records.inference: Showing the full document beside a fragment makes the missing local framing tangible. Keeping indexing recognizable isolates the change without implying a different final model.
records.rule: Highlight only changed information and operations. Never make generated context look like a verbatim source quotation.
records.limit: Do not move a preparation-time intervention to runtime. Added context is not automatic factual verification.

records.relationship: matched ablation; failure rate; common baseline
observed: Four bars compare standard and contextual groups; the visible values are 5.7, 5.0, 3.7 and 2.9.
The failure-rate scale starts at zero. A dotted divider separates condition groups, and subdued colors distinguish variants.
records.inference: Keeping the unfavorable direction explicit reduces the chance that taller bars are intuitively read as better. The lack of visible intervals must not be mistaken for zero uncertainty.
records.rule: Mark lower-is-better outcomes. Use a common scale for matched ablations and distinguish relative percentages from percentage points.
records.limit: Never reuse source benchmark values as a new topic's measurements. Do not invent confidence intervals or significance claims.

observed: The dark console retains the same general query and two-result structure but presents compact numbered rows.
The response is shorter through selected content, not merely reduced font size or a tighter crop.
records.inference: A matched query limits distracting changes and lets the reader inspect the actual contract difference. Concision is valuable when it preserves the next decision, not as an unconditional aesthetic preference.
records.rule: Keep query and result identity fixed in format comparisons. Reduce irrelevant information rather than making all text smaller.
records.limit: Do not infer token savings from image dimensions. Do not drop fields necessary for later actions merely to look clean.

observed: The console displays an invalid-identifier error with distinct sections for a summary, valid identifiers and resolution guidance.
Sectioned monospaced text provides an actionable next step rather than only a machine code.
records.inference: Visible recovery guidance makes the failure productive; an opaque error would force guessing or repeated invalid calls. The example counters an overly simplistic always-be-concise rule.
records.rule: Include actionable repair information in expected failure responses. Optimize for the next correct action, not merely text length.
records.limit: Do not invent a recovery command the tool cannot execute. Do not expose private account identifiers to make an example realistic.

records.relationship: opaque failure; contrast with actionable guidance
observed: The same general invalid-request situation appears as nested JSON with code, status, field and value.
The dark monospaced frame lacks the explanatory sections and recovery instructions visible in the companion error example.
records.inference: Holding the request and console frame stable isolates actionability. Treating JSON as inherently bad would be a mistaken stylistic generalization.
records.rule: Include counterexamples in a style library, not only attractive successes. Compare missing semantic affordances rather than blaming a serialization format.
records.limit: JSON may be appropriate for a wire protocol. Do not retrieve this negative example as an unqualified target style.

records.relationship: population share comparison; reference baseline; paired category
observed: Occupation rows connect coral Claude-conversation shares with dark workforce shares on one percentage axis.
Thin horizontal segments join paired dots and direct values identify endpoints; there are no filled bars and no arrowheads. Source alt text calls this a bar chart, which conflicts with the pixels.
records.inference: A dumbbell emphasizes the gap more efficiently than paired bars while retaining both baselines. The absence of arrows helps avoid implying a transition from one population into the other.
records.rule: Use connected dots when paired gaps, rather than totals, are the main question. Treat source alt-text mismatches as reviewable evidence discrepancies.
records.limit: Do not describe the segment as growth over time. Do not equate the share gap with the percentage of workers adopting AI.

observed: Two horizontal stacks use blue segments for one mode and purple segments for another, with legends to the right.
The top and bottom totals are approximately 57.4 and 42.6 rather than two independently normalized 100-percent bars.
records.inference: Unequal row lengths preserve the between-mode comparison while subdivision retains useful detail. Renormalizing each row would answer a different question and could conceal the main balance.
records.rule: Keep a shared denominator visible in grouped composition charts. Validate segment and group sums before rendering.
records.limit: Do not normalize each row to 100 percent without changing the explanation. Interaction mode is not a measured fraction of jobs replaced.

records.relationship: levels; file classes; loading conditions; size guidance
observed: A four-column table organizes levels, files, context-window conditions and token guidance across three rows.
Thin rules and gray cells dominate; a starred unlimited entry depends on explanatory context rather than a literal infinite model window.
records.inference: A restrained table permits precise cross-reading without decorative complexity. Preserving qualifications is essential because an isolated unlimited label is easy to misread.
records.rule: Choose tables for multi-attribute policy comparisons. Preserve footnotes that change the meaning of a cell.
records.limit: Do not interpret external material capacity as unlimited model context. Do not fabricate token budgets for a new domain.

records.relationship: outcome composition; training stages; uncertainty of interpretation
observed: Three panels combine paired stacked bars with a stacked-area training trajectory and a separate final bar.

Cyan, yellow and red-hatched regions distinguish refusal and different compliance-related categories; the hatch supplies a non-color cue. Fraction scales and internal condition labels organize the panels.
records.inference: Using both snapshots and a trajectory lets readers see endpoints and development. Patterning makes the highlighted behavioral category more accessible, but density requires careful legend placement.
records.rule: Use separate panels for condition comparisons and temporal trajectories. Add a pattern or label when a critical category must not depend on color alone.
records.limit: Do not turn these experimental frequencies into deployment incident rates. Do not merge distinct compliance categories merely to simplify the palette.

observed: A grid representing a codebase highlights a few salmon-colored cells among gray cells.
A question connects through a solid hand-drawn arrow to an orange-accented explanation card, while a dashed branch leads to a secondary artifact card. Contrasting summary bands sit below.
records.inference: Selective color concentrates attention before the explanatory handoff. A dashed secondary path can make optional depth visible without distracting from the primary answer, provided optionality is labeled.
records.rule: Show the selected scope before expanding it. Distinguish a primary answer from optional depth.
records.limit: Grid-cell count is not measured coverage or comprehension. Do not interpret a dashed optional branch as a failure path.

observed: A small input-pipeline-transcript overview is linked to a larger four-stage view of understanding, ideation, rollout and judgment.
Configuration labels sit near their owning stages. The rollout includes repeated turns and stopping choices; judge sliders appear as schematic outputs.
records.inference: A linked overview/detail layout lets readers orient first and inspect a complex stage second. Keeping stopping conditions inside the rollout avoids suggesting unlimited interaction.
records.rule: Use a linked overview and expansion rather than one overloaded diagram. Make iteration controls and stopping choices part of the explanation.
records.limit: Do not cite decorative slider positions as experimental outcomes. Do not present every possible rollout action as mandatory.

records.relationship: harness; suite; task; trial; grader; metric
observed: Nested rectangles organize an evaluation harness, suite and tasks, with stacked trial cards and distinct grader/metric chips.
An external agent-harness exchange and a separate outcome-to-grader path prevent all concepts from becoming one nested list.
records.inference: A hierarchy reduces the number of definitions readers must hold in memory. Extra cross-boundary edges show relationships that containment alone cannot express.
records.rule: Do not use containment to imply time order. Keep definitions, attempts, assessments and measurements distinct.
records.limit: A task is not a trial count. A recorded metric is not automatically a correct assessment.

observed: Three differently colored language lanes connect prompt forms to a shared gray concept region and then to corresponding output forms.
The displayed examples and explanatory wording contain a small opposite-of-large versus opposite-of-small wording inconsistency; this should not be copied into a new diagram.
records.inference: A common middle region makes reuse apparent at a glance. Retaining language lanes on either side helps readers follow which surface forms correspond without making the middle look language-specific.
records.rule: Use convergence/divergence to explain shared processing across surface variants. Check internal wording consistency even in an authoritative reference.
records.limit: One example does not establish a universal language-independent mechanism. A shared node label is not proof of complete equivalence between inputs.

records.relationship: scenario seeds; bounded auditing loop; multiple judgments
observed: Seed cards marked A, B and C appear on the left. A central auditing loop connects an auditor, a vertical tool menu and a target.
Judgment sliders on the right retain case markers, linking scenarios to several assessment dimensions.
records.inference: Repeated case markers support traceability across the pipeline. A large loop makes interaction central while the separate judge region prevents confusing generated behavior with its assessment.
records.rule: Preserve case identity across transformations. Distinguish an action menu from an ordered workflow.
records.limit: Do not imply every tool is invoked for every case. Do not cite illustrative slider values as benchmark findings.

observed: Three matched two-dimensional feature diagrams show increasing sparsity, labeled 0, 80 and 90 percent, with an arrow across the top.
Feature directions progress from fewer separated directions to denser arrangements; a feature-importance legend and interference annotation qualify the geometry.
records.inference: Matched planes permit direct comparison of geometric organization while a small number of features keeps the concept inspectable. The toy-model setting is an essential scope boundary.
records.rule: Use controlled small multiples to explain a geometric mechanism. Keep the numerical meaning of position and color tied to the model definition.
records.limit: Arbitrary categorical tasks cannot be drawn as mathematically orthogonal vectors without a defined model. A toy result is not a complete description of every deployed model.
